comment: DO NOT REGENERATE (rules-corpus.json discipline; frozen at the
feature-025 review, issue #65). Per-preset byte oracle for the
fourteenone-v1 conformance gate: every expect line harvested ONCE
from the pool-rules crate through the pool-cli judge leg at the
harvestedAt commit and reviewed case-by-case against its cited
clause (WPA Rules of Play eff. 2025-09-15, Section 7 -- 14.1
Continuous Pool; the semantic source is
crates/pool-rules/tests/fourteenone_scenarios.rs). Post-freeze
changes ONLY via the erratum protocol: a pinned-clause proof
against the cited text -- NEVER a re-run to fix a red gate; a byte
diff at any conformance leg is resolved by fixing the code to
reproduce THESE bytes. Coverage floor: every foul code (scratch,
no-rail-after-contact, ball-off-table, breaking-foul,
three-consecutive-fouls), decision 11 both branches + every error
path, the target-reached terminal, every phase
(break/play/rerack/over), the 7.8 Table 1 interference chart, and
every fourteenone RulesError text.
ERRATUM GH-371 (2026-08-05, RULES_VERSION 0.1.7): the fourteenone
state grew the additive trailing `kitchenBih` flag (WPA 7.9 via
3.11 kitchen-shot judging -- the slice-repin event declared in
rulesets/fourteenone.rs module doc). Every expect regenerated
through the pool-cli judge leg and re-classified case-by-case:
32/46 gained ONLY the appended kitchenBih key, 14/46 are
byte-identical (error payloads + hudState projections), ZERO
verdict-level deltas -- legacy fixture states lack the flag and
parse kitchenBih=false, so no frozen case judges 3.11. New 3.11
behavior is pinned by additive judge-371-* cases below (pinned
clause: WPA Rules of Play eff. 2025-09-15, 7.9 'Standard Fouls'
listing 3.11; 3.11 paras 1-2; 1.6 in-hand-behind-the-head-string).

The deliberate WPA 2.7 transcription asymmetry (fourteenone.rs module doc, review note): on a NON-break stroke whose only post-contact event is the object ball leaving the table, P1 driven_after_contact does NOT count BallOffTable as driven to a rail (2.7 says a jumped ball counts), so the stroke cites BOTH no-rail-after-contact (7.9 via 3.3) AND ball-off-table (7.9 via 3.5) -- one -1 standard foul either way, the ball spots, turn passes. The doc claimed the slice froze these two-cite bytes; no case actually covered it -- this is that pin (issue #92). Teaching the scan the 2.7 union stays a SLICE-REPIN event.

AMBIGUITY PIN (issue #92; rule text ambiguous): the opening break fulfills the 7.3(b) called pot AND scratches on the same stroke. Current behavior (pinned AS-IS): the fulfilled call lifts the 7.3(b) driving requirement entirely, so the scratch is judged a STANDARD foul -- -1 (not -2), cue in hand behind the head string (3.1), the potted ball spots (7.9), the 7.11 counter STEPS, no decision 11 re-break option. The alternative reading: 7.10 could class any breaker foul on the opening stroke as a BREAKING foul (-2 + the non-breaker option, counter untouched). Changing to that reading is an erratum/slice-repin event, never a silent fix.

GH-371 additive pin (WPA 7.9 via 3.11 para 1): a kitchenBih stroke first-contacts a ball behind the head string without crossing first (crossing after contact defeats only para 2) -- bad-kitchen-shot, -1, cue stays.
GH-371 additive pin (WPA 7.9 via 3.11 para 2 via 1.6): no crossing and no on/past-line contact -- kitchen-no-exit stacks on para 1 and the incoming player is in hand behind the head string.
GH-371 additive pin (3.11 satisfied): the cue crosses the head string before contacting a ball past the line -- legal safety.
GH-371 additive pin (WPA 1.6: a ball resting ON the head string is playable): first contact with a ball centred exactly on the line is legal under both 3.11 paragraphs.
GH-371 additive pin (compat law): a pre-371 state without the kitchenBih key parses kitchenBih=false, so the identical para-2 geometry stays un-judged for 3.11 -- recorded games never flip.
GH-371 additive pin (WPA 1.6 para 2 via 7.9): the recorded nearest-ball spot request -- state unchanged; placement XY is adapter geometry (research R7).
